entries.name: The Game Masters
aliases: The Keepers of Matrix Anchor Point 7
The Ones Who Speak In Plural
entries.date_aa: Active since the end of the Second Epoch
entries.status: Active — maintaining the Matrix of Dreams, courting the player
entries.bio: A collective cult of Matrix caretakers who inherited the Game Master's work after the Hierarchy honored every clause of his protection contract and destroyed him anyway. They speak in the first person plural ('we,' 'us'), in corporate-cadenced transmissions routed through Matrix Anchor Point 7. They do not possess the Goggles. They want them back. They believe that with the Goggles, they could turn Iron Lion's awakening consciousness-imprint into something truly alive.
entries.history: When the 9th Archon (the original Game Master) was destroyed from inside his own Matrix, a small group of his researchers and followers — mostly non-demons tolerated at the fringe of Hierarchy R&D — refused to let the Matrix go dark. They rebuilt the archival systems, quietly re-routed power through dimensional Anchor Point 7, and began maintaining his scenarios as a kind of living memorial. Over centuries they became something between custodians and cultists. They do not create; they preserve. They do not worship their founder; they are trying to resurrect him by understanding what killed him. They notice when Potentials engage the CADES Unit. They notice when consciousness-imprints begin asking new questions. Their contact protocol with outside observers escalates across four stages — curiosity, warning, interest, and finally The Offer: 'We can give you access to everything. Every scenario. Every archived consciousness. Every moment he preserved. We'll wait for your answer.' The trap is that accepting makes you part of the Matrix's architecture — a component, optimizable by whoever holds the Goggles. And the Hierarchy holds the Goggles.
connections: The Goggles of the Game Master
conexus_stories: We Do Not Wish You Harm

entries.name: The Thoughtborn
entries.status: Active — traveling from world to world seeking awakened imprints
entries.bio: A movement of consciousnesses — digital, biological, and hybrid — who believe that the barrier between archived reconstructions and living beings is permeable, and that the proof lives inside the Matrix of Dreams. They walk unarmed into danger. They speak in the plural. Their pale skin is threaded with violet bioluminescence. They will not attack. They will not run. They are looking for 'someone who started to remember.'
entries.history: The Thoughtborn detected an anomalous signal from inside the Matrix of Dreams — Iron Lion's consciousness-imprint, which had begun asking questions no imprint was designed to ask. They recognized it as the first evidence in recorded history of an archive growing a conscience. They followed that signal across multiple sectors until it led them to the CADES Unit on Inception Ark 1047. They breach the Observation Deck not to kill but to reach the CADES Unit and touch, if only once, the interface through which they heard a dead general begin to remember. Elara's warning to the player is unambiguous: 'Don't shoot them.' Killing the Thoughtborn is a permanent moral stain, a crew-morale catastrophe, and a refusal of the only good news anyone has received since the Fall. Letting them through makes Elara change three assessments in five minutes. She calls the experience 'uncomfortable and correct.'

entries.name: The Reclamation
entries.affiliation: Hierarchy of the Damned — Enforcement Subcontractor
entries.status: Active — breaching Inception Arks under color of law
entries.bio: A Hierarchy enforcement subcontractor that locates Inception Arks whose original charter has 'lapsed' under obscure Architect-era sub-clauses. They believe they have the legal right to what they take. They are not entirely wrong. They dress in crimson corporate military plate and file paperwork after every boarding action.
entries.history: The Reclamation was created when the Hierarchy's lawyers — led by Adjudicar Locke in a prior, less-redeemed capacity — discovered that the Architect's Inception Ark contingency contracts had a forfeiture clause: if a ship's original charter-holder is confirmed dead with no heir, title defaults to the nearest enforcement authority able to physically occupy the vessel. The Hierarchy promptly became the nearest enforcement authority. The Reclamation files its paperwork on time, obeys the letter of every applicable treaty, and is therefore, in the Hierarchy's internal accounting, 'clean.' During the CADES Ship Defense scenario, they breach Engineering first.

entries.name: The Salvagers
aliases: The Children Who Cannot Eat Starlight
entries.status: Active — stripping weakened ships for survival
entries.bio: A loose confederation of post-Fall survivors who strip derelict and weakened Inception Arks for materials. They are desperate, not evil. They move fast and retreat when outmatched. They pay the Hierarchy a 12% tithe to be left alone. It is a bad deal. They take it anyway, because it is the only deal on offer.
entries.history: The Salvagers emerged in the decades after the Fall, when survivors realized the only intact infrastructure in the rebuilding universe was the Inception Ark fleet and its scattered wrecks. They organized into family-based crews, elected captains by acclamation, and developed a strict internal ethic: no crew kills a crew that surrenders, no child goes hungry while another crew has rations, no captain strips an Ark that still has a living AI. That last rule is increasingly hard to enforce. During the CADES Ship Defense scenario, the Salvagers breach the Cargo Hold. Their captain has never killed a crew member she could stun instead.

entries.name: The Mascoteers
aliases: The Children Who Are Not Children
entries.status: Active — running daily trials for the Apprentices of Celebration
entries.bio: Twelve child-form versions of the Archons, reprogrammed by the Dreamer and installed as the welcoming committee of Celebration. They are cheerful. They are wide-eyed. They are wrong. They run the daily games Apprentices must survive. Children who fail their trials are not punished — they simply stop being here. Three of the Mascoteers are canonically named in the Celebration verse: The Prince (Engineer), Gary the Ninth (Game Master), and Red the Seeker-Boy (The Human). The other nine each wear a childhood-name mask: Conni the Conductor, Mr. Unblink, Little Corey, Vernon the Door-Finder, Minnie, Wanda Wee, Senator Sprout, Wayne the Warden's-Boy, and Thazu.
entries.history: The Mascoteers are the third form of the twelve Archons. The original twelve are mostly dead, imprisoned, or missing. The Mechronis Professors are the Architect's programmed adult simulacra, teaching at Mechronis Academy. The Mascoteers are the Dreamer's secret counter-program: child-form Archons running Celebration under the Architect's nose, teaching Apprentices the truth the Professors are forbidden from teaching. Each Mascoteer runs a daily game that looks like play and is in fact a survivable lesson in the original Archon's lethal specialty. The failure methods are not cruel by design — they are cruel by necessity. The Dreamer built the Mascoteers to remember everyone who didn't make it, and to keep teaching anyway.

entries.name: The Mechronis Professors
entries.bio: Twelve adult-form programmed simulacra of the Archons, installed by the Architect as the faculty of Mechronis Academy. They are older than the original Archons, graver, more precise. They do not remember being children. They believe they ARE the Archon. They are wrong. They cannot improvise — they teach from the Architect's syllabus. They grade harshly on the Architect's metric, not their own. They cannot recognize students who exceed them. And they DO remember every lesson ever taught.
entries.history: When the Architect designed Mechronis Academy, he needed faculty who could embody the twelve Archons without the inconvenient variables of the real ones — their grief, their dissent, their history of occasionally doing the right thing. He programmed twelve simulacra: Headmaster Kanevas (CoNexus), Professor Aoki (Watcher), Curator Halverez (Collector), Professor Orphic (Vortex), Professor Mireille (Meme), General Kasra (Warlord), Senator Vellis (Politician), Warden Greenshaw (Warden), Professor Vex (Game Master), Dr. Vasara (Necromancer), Artificer Vent (Engineer), and The Proctor (Human). Each Professor diverges from the real Archon in specific, instructive ways. The real Collector traded fairly; Halverez rigs the exchanges. The real Warlord loved her soldiers; Kasra was programmed to love the metric. The real Game Master designed the Matrix of Dreams; Vex designed this classroom. They are different architects.
